frontmatter.title: Should you do a master's at all? The counterfactual most guides skip
frontmatter.scope: When a pre-experience business master's adds value and when it doesn't, by country norm and target career, compared with working straight after a bachelor's, apprenticeships and dual study, professional qualifications, or a later MBA. Assembled from figures already verified in this library, plus Dale & Krueger on selection effects. The topic was suggested by the Gemini library (v2/breadth/no-master-counterfactual.md), whose figures were not reused.
frontmatter.confidence: medium. The country norms and career-specific rules are well sourced. No study directly measures the master's premium for European business graduates net of selection, so the overall verdict is a reasoned synthesis.

frontmatter.title: Student logistics — cash on day zero, deposits, work limits, health cover and permits
frontmatter.scope: The practical constraints that make otherwise-sound plans fail: upfront visa and health charges, rental deposits, proof of funds, student work-hour limits, health insurance, and the Swiss and French permit details that matter for non-EU students. Only rules verified on official pages are stated as facts; others are flagged. The topic was suggested by the Gemini library (v2/breadth/student-logistics.md and the red-team audit); its figures were re-checked, and several were outdated or wrong.
frontmatter.confidence: medium. Each stated rule was read on an official page on 2026-09-30/10-01, but coverage is partial (UK, Germany, France, Switzerland in depth; others flagged).

frontmatter.title: How schools, rankings and the press mislead with numbers — a field guide with verified examples
frontmatter.scope: The statistical fallacies, reporting conventions and biases that make business-school marketing, rankings and press coverage look better (or scarier) than the underlying reality. Each item gives the mechanism, a real example verified against its primary source, how to detect it, and the question to ask. It also sets out Admetia's own reporting standard and a correction log. Basis for the site's "Fact-check desk". It complements decisions/school-types-and-accreditation.md and money/salari
frontmatter.confidence: high for the examples (each re-checked against the primary document named); medium for the size of the biases, which are rarely measurable from outside.

frontmatter.title: Decision framework — the order of decisions for a pre-experience business master's and first career
frontmatter.scope: Cross-cutting synthesis of the 17 research files in /research. It sets the order in which a student should make the decisions (constraints → career → country → programme → school → timing → money → execution) and gives decision rules for each step, plus cross-career comparison tables and the myths that most often derail students. Evidence lives in the source files. This file cites the file, plus the key primary source where one figure carries a rule.
frontmatter.confidence: medium. The ordering and most rules rest on figures that were spot-checked against primary sources (see _working/progress.md). Rules marked (thin) rest on single sources or practitioner consensus.

frontmatter.title: Country brief: Saudi Arabia
frontmatter.scope: Where a European business or computing graduate should look in Saudi Arabia (Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam and Dhahran): the economy, the localisation rules, the regional-headquarters programme, named employers, who the graduate schemes are for, hub standing at national, Middle East and world scale, and the evidence behind it. Visas and entry are in the Atlas record and places/visas-and-work-rights.md. Information only; not legal, tax or immigration advice.
frontmatter.confidence: medium; rankings, labour statistics and the localisation rules are published, but nothing on entry pay or graduate hiring by city exists, the Kingdom publishes no regional GDP or wage series, and the regional-headquarters counts are from news reports

frontmatter.title: Management consulting careers for pre-experience master's graduates
frontmatter.scope: Entry routes, hiring trends 2023–26, pay by city, selection, internships, languages, exits and culture in management consulting (MBB, tier-2 strategy, Big 4 consulting, Accenture, boutiques, in-house) for MiM/MSc graduates, Europe-first with the US for comparison. Excludes the month-by-month recruiting calendar (see getting-in/recruiting-calendar.md), visas (see places/visas-and-work-rights.md) and cross-sector salary ROI (see money/salaries-and-roi.md).
frontmatter.confidence: medium, because entry structure, languages, selection and trend facts come from firm pages and on-the-record press, but city pay relies on aggregator and self-reported data and Middle East access, Southern European offices and exits could not be sourced from primary pages

frontmatter.title: Verification round 3d (P2, P13, P17: IBD degree mix, sponsorship odds by employer type, internship-to-full-time conversion)
frontmatter.scope: Primary-source verification of three weak claims from verification/claims-to-verify.md section 4. P2 is the IBD-only degree mix (finance vs STEM vs other) in London and European analyst classes, 2024-26. P13 is sponsorship odds by employer type and evidence that needing a visa lowers hiring odds. P17 is summer-internship-to-full-time conversion in London investment banking. Log of what each source says, status, and every edit to body files. frontmatter.scope: When to do what. Master's straight after the bachelor's vs working first, gap and internship years, a second master's, MiM now and MBA later (including deferred-MBA programmes), a business PhD as an alternative, age norms and experience caps, and graduating into a downturn. Excludes detailed visa rules (see places/visas-and-work-rights.md), application and recruiting dates (see getting-in/recruiting-calendar.md, getting-in/admissions.md), costs (see money/costs-and-funding.md) and salary leve
frontmatter.confidence: medium - eligibility rules and deferred-MBA terms come from school pages read today, but outcome effects of timing rest on academic studies from North America (mostly pre-2023) and few school reports split outcomes by prior experience
